findings.description: The plan requires exact commands for Firebase deploy and realtime smoke ActionItems, but the shipped ActionItem constructor validates exact_command against the known DontPanic command vocabulary. The plan does not say whether those external Firebase commands become validated operator-only commands, wrapper commands, or a new validated command class, so the catalog can fail at construction or silently lose the exact command outcome.

Adding SOURCE_INTEGRATION and provide_integration_actions() is not enough to prove the standard operator surfaces render the items. The shipped dashboard collection path explicitly aggregates each provider and maintains per-source scope and freshness maps; the plan does not require wiring the new provider through that real collect_state/dashboard.build/write_cache path.

F002 says the static smoke captures run output as an evidence ref, while F004 consumes evidence refs to flip status, but no feature pins the evidence storage location, schema, write API, or clears_when predicate input. Without that contract, the smoke can pass and still fail the completion test requiring status to change without hand-editing.

F004's description correctly says there is no separate integrations panel and status must route through shipped what-now/operator-console surfaces, but its steps still instruct implementation to render a dashboard integrations panel. That contradicts the objective contract and can lock a UI path the source-of-truth decision explicitly removed.

The plan names statuses configured, deployed, smoke-passing, and pending, but it does not pin the per-integration matrix mapping catalog entries and evidence refs to each status. Firebase, static dashboard, Linear, and Discord have different evidence shapes, so two implementations could satisfy the prose while linking or clearing different pending items.

F003 says deploy and realtime-smoke items render gated or unavailable until trigger and credentials are present, but the trigger source and credential-presence semantics are not pinned. That leaves room for hiding gated items, probing real secrets, or making visibility depend on live environment state, all of which conflict with offline fixture proof and no-secret rendering.

F002 says the static smoke verifies exported artifacts are present and parseable, but the journey and completion test require proof that the static dashboard actually renders those artifacts. Parseable JSON can still fail the dashboard loader or render path, so this can pass while missing the user-facing outcome.

The plan depends on operator-attested integration-evidence records to meet Firebase trigger conditions and clear external deploy, realtime smoke, Linear, and Discord items, but it does not define a user-facing capture path for those attestations. Without an explicit offline command or workflow, operators may have to hand-edit evidence files, contradicting the no-hand-editing resolution contract.

F004 says resolved integrations clear via clears_when while also promising configured, deployed, and smoke-passing readiness at a glance through existing what-now/operator-console surfaces. Because there is no separate integrations panel, the plan must pin what remains visible after pending ActionItems clear; otherwise successful integrations can disappear instead of surfacing their derived status.

The plan introduces operator_command, credentials_required, evidence_expected, and trigger_condition, but the shipped ActionItem envelope and dashboard normalizers currently use a closed set of serialized fields and source labels. F001 requires real rendering, but does not explicitly require these new display fields to survive ActionItem.to_dict, triage, what-now, and operator-console normalization.

The status matrix says stale or failed evidence keeps the integration at its prior floor, but the evidence contract is a JSON file per integration and does not define how prior successful evidence is preserved when a later failed record is written. Two implementations could overwrite success, silently regress, or ignore failure while still matching the current prose.

The plan requires exact credential requirements, but the proposed catalog mostly pins credentials_required as a boolean and does not lock the per-item env-var name list or display shape. Without a deterministic list of credential names, offline fixture checks and operator-facing setup guidance can pass while still failing to tell the operator what credentials are required.

F003 says gated Firebase deploy and realtime-smoke items always render, while F004 says only genuinely pending integrations occupy the needs-action band. The plan does not pin the band/status behavior for unmet triggers, so an implementation could either hide the item or incorrectly show not-yet-needed Firebase work as needing action.

F002 tests the smoke writer and F004 tests status derivation with fixtures, but the plan does not require the completion-test path where the rendered static-dashboard ActionItem exact_command is executed, writes evidence, and then the real provider-to-render rebuild flips that integration's status without hand-editing.

The plan conflicts on the source of truth for configured status: F002 says downstream consumers read only append-only evidence files, while the F004 matrix derives some configured states from env-var name presence. That can clear or advance integration status without captured evidence.

The trigger condition for Firebase deploy/realtime work is met only by operator-attested evidence, but the attest command is specified only as integration/outcome/note and does not pin an action identifier or trigger-record type.

Post-clear visibility is not mechanically pinned against the shipped clears_when suppression model. A pending item that clears via clears_when will be suppressed unless the plan defines a separate quiet status item or a band-transform path.
The static-dashboard smoke acceptance says rendered artifacts must exist, but artifact existence alone is weaker than render-proof and may not fail parseable-but-unrenderable dashboard state.

The proposed source/provider wiring pins the main build path, but the standard dashboard can also flow through fleet/project projection rehydration, where unknown sources and new display fields can be filtered or dropped.

The proposal says to enumerate catalog entries, exact operator commands, credential env-var names, and evidence expectations, but it does not pin the actual catalog rows before implementation. The core outcome depends on those literals being truthful and deterministic, so leaving them to implementation risks command drift and inconsistent fixture expectations.

F002 defines the attestation CLI syntax but does not pin the runnable static-dashboard smoke command that F001 must render as the ActionItem exact_command and F004 must execute in the end-to-end status-flip test. Without the literal command shape, the completion test cannot prove the rendered action is the one that writes evidence.

The render-proof smoke can still be under-specified if marker checks are allowed to pass by finding exported values in copied state JSON rather than in an actual dashboard-rendered artifact. The user journey requires verifying artifacts render, not merely that export-dashboard produced readable state files.

The plan says clears_when names or reads integration evidence files, but it does not pin the closed predicate registry entry, predicate parameters, or action-specific matching semantics. Since shipped clears_when is predicate-based rather than arbitrary file-based, pending action clearing and status-item persistence remain ambiguous.

F003 refers to rendering untriggered gated items in the QUIET band, but the shipped ActionItem band vocabulary is needs_action, advisory, info, and ready; quiet is an operator-triage bucket concept. This vocabulary mismatch can break provider construction or produce inconsistent what-now versus operator-console rendering.

The gated deploy/realtime plan pins untriggered and actionable states, but it does not fully specify the trigger-met-but-credentials-absent state. Credential requirements are central to the user journey, and the operator must see whether the item is waiting on trigger evidence, credential provisioning, or post-credential execution.

F004 says each integration emits two items, but F001 requires one ActionItem per catalog action step. Firebase functions has separate credential and deploy steps, so a two-items-per-integration rule would either collapse distinct pending actions or conflict with the completion test's one-truthful-ActionItem-per-step requirement.

The Firebase trigger is defined as action_id firebase-trigger, but the catalog does not make it a visible operator action or otherwise provide the exact attestation command that satisfies the trigger. The operator can see the gated deploy/realtime items but lacks a first-class, rendered path to mark multi-operator need as met.

F003 intentionally renders trigger-unmet deploy/realtime items as info, and F004 renders status items as info, but the shipped operator-console triage path treats info/advisory as quiet and the default console only shows needs_auth, needs_decision, and uncertain. The plan does not pin how these always-visible integration items appear in the standard operator-console surface.

The render-proof smoke says it runs the real dashboard build over export-dashboard output and checks built rendered artifacts, but it does not pin the actual render mechanism. For a static SPA, copied state JSON and static build output can diverge from browser-rendered DOM, so the smoke could remain parse-proof rather than render-proof.

The status matrix says a later failed record surfaces a failure flag without regressing the status floor, but it does not define record ordering or malformed-record handling. Captured timestamps, JSONL append order, duplicate records, and unknown action_ids can produce different derived statuses unless the deterministic rule is pinned.

reason: All round-5 findings resolved by concrete artifact edits recorded in D008 (literal catalog table, literal smoke command, built-artifact markers, registered clears_when predicate, shipped band vocabulary, creds-absent state). Rounds 1-4 cleared 100% with 19 findings resolved by artifact edits (D003-D007); round 5 was matrix-pin/vocabulary class with 2 of 3 highs streak-unlocked as waivable by the convergence policy itself. Override per the operator's standing lock protocol (dispositions/override once findings are implementation-detail pins against explicit contracts); it skips only re-verification of resolutions already made.
